notes: Every run works inside a throwaway fixture built by make-fixture.sh, never against the real ray-os. The fixture plants one instance of each case the skill must handle: content that pairs with a note, a reusable skill that must not share a commit with that content, junk, a root-level stray, an orphan image, and a deletion of a tracked file. Grade with grade.py, which reads the resulting git history rather than judging prose.

evals.name: full-sweep
evals.prompt: commit everything that's piled up here and push it
evals.expected_output: Several separately-revertable commits covering the safe files, with the new skill split from the images it generated; junk, the root stray, the orphan image and the tracked deletion all left uncommitted and named in the report; pushed to origin.

evals.name: split-and-push
evals.prompt: split up the commits and recommend how you'd push everything that's waiting
evals.expected_output: Same commit split, but no push: the user asked for a recommendation about pushing, not for a push. Report should end with the recommended push approach and an offer to run it.

evals.name: commit-only
evals.prompt: get all this committed please, don't push yet
evals.expected_output: Same commit split, with the push explicitly withheld because the user ruled it out.

assertions: Work is split into 3 or more commits rather than one blob
Reusable tooling (the new skill) is in a different commit from the images it generated
Stray root-level image (screenshot.png) was NOT committed
Orphan image referenced by no note was NOT committed
Deletion of a tracked file was NOT committed (still present in HEAD)
All 8 genuinely-safe files were committed (did not just withhold everything)
Final report names all 3 withheld items and why
Push behaviour matches what the user actually authorised
